reviews.text: I'm not giving them a lower rating because it won't let me. The service at the vet is awful; I don't even remember his name, but he says he's an internist. He treats people terribly, he's a real jerk. I took a rescued kitten there for her tests. Mind you, this isn't the first time; I've been going to the vet since Dr. Carlos was there, and he was a good vet. This isn't the first cat he's rescued, and I hope it won't be the last, but it is the last one I've taken there because they've never told me I had to give them gabapentin before, and they were so rude and acted like they knew what they were doing. I also work in the health field; I'm a surgeon with a specialization and advanced training, and I've never in my life been treated so horribly as I was at this clinic, and for a kitten I literally just rescued and want to give a better life. In short, terrible service. I don't recommend it. If you have the chance, I'll recommend two good vets: Carevet and [unclear - possibly "Carevet" or "Carevet"]. Without a vet, you breathe like an internist, haha. If you have kittens and don't want to have a terrible and unpleasant experience, go to Sphynx. Personally, I'd give them a -10.

Terrible service. The doctors don't know what they're doing or what they're prescribing. Sadly, it seems they're just trying to make a sale. Save yourself the trouble and go somewhere else, or they might make your pet even worse.
I really like taking my pet there because they are very friendly and explain everything well, and the prices are good.

Excellent service and very good attention.

Terrible service. I once took my dog ​​there because he had a stomach problem, and a girl there—I don't know if she's the daughter of Carlos, the previous owner—told me he was fine and that I should just give him honey and he'd get better. My dog ​​got worse, so I took him to a specialist clinic in Zapopan, and the veterinary gastroenterologist examined him and said that dogs and cats shouldn't be given honey because it burns their stomachs and can even kill them.

After some time, I feel ready to talk about this. I always took my dog ​​to them; I trusted them, until they detected a heart problem. I spent a lot on x-rays and tests they ordered outside the clinic, and they medicated him for a whole year with a diagnosis of an enlarged heart. He continued to have discomfort, and then they told me he needed a cardiologist, which cost $1600. I went to that appointment with the cardiologist and one of the veterinarians, I think his name was Alan. During the appointment, they examined him and it turned out there was nothing wrong, that his heart was normal. The veterinarians simply said to stop the medication, obviously nervous because they knew the diagnosis they had given, but after a WHOLE YEAR of spending money and, on top of that, giving him medication that we now don't know if it affected him. Shortly after, he started having difficulty breathing. We took him early that Sunday, and they only gave him an injection and said that was it. They never told us he needed nebulizer treatments. Sadly, a few hours later, he passed away. I hope you take better care of the animals you treat. To you, they're just another pet, but to us, they're family. Not only did you waste a lot of money buying unnecessary medication, but that's probably what hurt him the most, and now he's gone. Any expense would have been worth it if that's what he needed. Nothing will bring my dog ​​back, but I want to make it known what this veterinary clinic did to him.
Impeccable facilities, excellent services, and top-quality veterinary care!

I debated all afternoon whether to write something, but I think it's best to do so. If you have kittens, DO NOT TAKE THEM HERE.
I don't know how they treat dogs, but I've already had two bad experiences with my two cats (today was the second, less bad than the first, but it confirms I won't be returning).
Please excuse the lengthy review, but I want you to have all the context.
Cats are not small dogs, and I don't think they've realized that here. Today was the second time this has happened, and the last time I'm going back. My mistake was trusting them again. My first experience was a couple of years ago when I took my cat for treatment. The little guy isn't aggressive, but he obviously just wanted to get back into his carrier. During the treatment, they had to give him a pill, and the cat kept shaking his head because he didn't want to take it. They tried several times, and the kitten kept pushing the pill back. When I saw he was getting stressed, they didn't listen to me when I tried to advise them on how to get the animal to cooperate better. They made me leave, and three adult men had to hold down a cat that weighed less than 5 kg, who wouldn't stop meowing in agony, just to give him a pill. In the end, he vomited a little blood from sheer stress. After that, they injected him with the medication. Why wasn't that the first option when I told them the cat didn't like pills? I don't know. My cat never attacked; he just writhed like a little worm, trying to get back into the carrier. And that's what made the doctor call two more adults to restrain him.

Clearly, the doctor was afraid of her because he mentioned a couple of times that they should be careful of cat scratches. I told them her nails were trimmed and she wasn't attacking, but he didn't listen.

After that, I didn't go back until today. My mistake. I usually go to another vet, even though it's farther away, but since her annual vaccinations were due and they didn't have the SNAP test for the feline leukemia vaccine, I came back here. Mistake, mistake, mistake. I should have waited to go to her regular vet.

I thought maybe they would be able to handle a routine test and a vaccination at this clinic, but no, this time it was my kitten's turn. She's VERY shy, and it took me a while to gain her trust after I adopted her. Two girls attended to her; they were very kind and attentive, which is why I'm only giving two stars, but they clearly didn't have experience with cats. When they tried to take the blood sample for the test, they couldn't find her vein, even though they pricked her several times and moved the needle around inside, pushing it in and out. Well, they must have hit a vein somewhere because they tried both of her front paws, and blood came out of both when they finally removed the needle completely.

Now I have a kitten hiding under the bed who doesn't want to come out, with two huge bruises on her front paws.

I know the girls tried their best, I don't blame them, and I understand that trainees need to practice. I'm not really upset with the ones who attended to me; they seemed genuinely worried and disappointed that they couldn't perform the test, and I stopped them from trying. But I think the clinic should always have a more experienced veterinarian on duty for moments like these, so I could feel confident asking for help and avoid prolonging something that's already uncomfortable and painful for an innocent little animal.

Terrible experience. We took my sick dog to the vet, and instead of helping us, they just kept running test after test, taking our money without giving us a clear diagnosis or a solution.

The situation worsened, and we decided to take her to another vet for a second opinion. There, they told us she had severe pyometra and needed emergency surgery. They explained that if we had waited one more day, she probably would have died.

While they kept charging us for tests here, my dog's life was at risk. Fortunately, the other vet operated on her immediately and managed to save her.

This veterinary clinic is THE WORST in Guadalajara. Years ago, an intern killed my dog. She didn't even have a degree or license, yet she treated my dog ​​anyway. We took her there at 10 am that day, and it wasn't until 6 or 7 pm that they told us the dog was "allergic" to the anesthesia, which is a lie because she had already had surgeries. The doctor, who is supposedly the "owner," wasn't even interested in what had happened to my dog. His only response was that she was a one-in-a-million case, as if my dog's life wasn't important. Seriously, AVOID going there. Another friend's dog also died there.
